page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ads_v5 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 614 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2702.98, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core CPU performance and memory read bandwidth are average, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 10806.97 and cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 514.43 GB/sec. However, large-block memory write bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 22.49 GB/sec. Large-model LLM prompt processing is also weak, processing 17.35 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model, though small 135M model inference remains average.

Given the high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU and the inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and memory-bound applications. The lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses and the lower multi-core scaling should be factored into deployment architectures.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8ads_v5 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 614 GB local SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers strong single-core CPU performance, though its multi-core performance and large-block memory write bandwidth are average to weak. With a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core, it provides a balanced profile for memory-heavy workloads. It is highly suited for database operations, web serving, and memory-bound enterprise applications that benefit from local SSD storage and premium storage capabilities, while avoiding workloads dependent on high-speed multi-threaded memory writes.
